title: normalize_uri drops an empty authority (file:///x -> file:/x)
property: normalizing a URI preserves its component structure; an empty-but-present authority stays '//'
evidence: RFC 3986 section 5.3 recomposition: if authority is defined (even empty), append '//' + authority. Docstring says normalize_uri equals uri_reference(uri).normalize().unsplit(); normalization (6.2.2) must not change the URI's meaning. unsplit() uses truthiness of authority, so '//' is lost (also '//' -> '').

title: normalize_uri turns a '//'-leading path into an authority
property: normalized URI re-parses with the same authority presence as the input
expected: a path of '//b' with no authority (e.g. 'a:/.//b' or 'a:/%2F...' style form); result must not re-parse with authority 'b'
actual: 'a://b', which parses as scheme 'a', authority 'b', no path
evidence: RFC 3986 section 3.3: when no authority is present the path cannot begin with '//'; section 6.2.2 normalization must be semantics-preserving. remove_dot_segments produces '//b' and unsplit() concatenates it directly after 'a:'.
